problem: Existing VLN methods (e.g., DUET) feed whole instructions into Transformers without exploiting fine-grained object and action phrases, and they fuse image-object features with text without modeling object relations across modalities.
motivation: Key actions and target objects in instructions are easily overlooked, and objects seen in the environment are tightly linked to objects named in the instruction. Modeling these links explicitly should improve navigation decisions and object grounding, without relying on external knowledge bases (unlike KERM).
key_idea: Extract object and action phrases from the instruction and use them to enhance text features, and separately model object-level image and text-object features with a cross-modal encoder, all on top of the DUET baseline.
insight: Both the text-side and vision-side object enhancements help on REVERIE val-unseen, and they are complementary. SR goes from 46.98 (baseline) to 49.47 (TSE+TOPA), 50.01 (IOPA) and 51.72 (both). The OPE gated multi-head attention matters: the full model without OPE reaches SR 47.37 versus 51.72 with it, so naive addition of the modules barely helps. Gains are largest on REVERIE test-unseen, where object grounding matters most.
method: Object and Action Parser (TSE): uses spaCy POS tagging plus a DistilBERT tokenizer with a hand-defined action vocabulary to extract action verbs and object nouns (lemmatized, cleaned). The object phrases, action phrases and the original instruction are each embedded in 768-d with positional embeddings.
TOPA: BERT encodes the instruction into E_c. Multi-head attention between E_c and the [object, action] phrase embeddings gives E_g. A sigmoid gate mixes them: A_f = w*E_g + (1-w)*E_c.
OPE (Object Perception-Enhancement): the MHA plus gated-fusion block used inside TOPA and IOPA to emphasize object and action information.

IOPA image features: CLIP features for panorama views and objects are modeled jointly by self-attention. Object features get two position embeddings (relative to the start node and to neighboring nodes).

Fine-grained cross-modal encoder: an LXMERT-style encoder fuses object features with text-object embeddings I_o to give O_bar, and fuses panorama+object features with TOPA-enhanced text to give f_t. MHA plus a gate then combine O_bar and f_t into the final image features A_f^R.
Dynamic fusion: as in DUET, a coarse global action score and a fine local score (converted to global space) are weighted-fused to pick the next node.

setting.backbone: DUET-based dual-scale graph Transformer (BERT text encoder, CLIP-B/16 visual features, LXMERT-style cross-modal encoders), trained end to end
setting.training_data: R2R and REVERIE training sets with pretraining via MLM, MRC, SAP (plus OG on REVERIE); EnvEdit-augmented features used; no other extra data reported
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (CLIP features), GPS/relative position, provided object bounding boxes on REVERIE
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints on a dynamically built topological map
setting.privileged: GT object bounding boxes provided by REVERIE (standard for the benchmark)

numbers_note: R2R metrics are printed as integers for SR/SPL/OSR. Ablations (Tables 3-4, REVERIE val-unseen) are not included as separate entries.
results: DOPE beats its DUET baseline on R2R test-unseen (NE 3.06 vs 3.65, SR 74 vs 69, SPL 63 vs 59) and is on par with or slightly above BEVBert. On REVERIE test-unseen it reaches SR 58.38, SPL 41.87 and RGS 35.84, above CONSOLE (SR 55.13) and ACK (SR 53.97). On REVERIE val-unseen it is roughly tied with BEVBert on SR and SPL.
limitations: Built on DUET with hand-crafted POS/vocabulary-based phrase extraction, which may miss complex or implicit object references; there is no analysis of parser errors.
Only evaluated on R2R and REVERIE in the discrete simulator, with no continuous-environment or real-robot tests.
Gains over the strongest baselines on R2R are small (about 1 point), and the very high dropout (0.7) is tuned on the REVERIE val-unseen split.
